balance_notes: GDD 2.5, full hold roughly doubles the ship at base storage. Computed the way the crew computes it: spawn-weighted across the shipping slice (bottom and middle thirds, hand-tetherable only, non-fragile crushing at compactor_tier 1) the catalog runs 19.66 kg per slot, so 6 base slots is 117.9 kg. dry_mass_kg 108 gives (108 + 117.9) / 108 = 2.09, inside the 25% window with room either side. dry_mass_kg moved 96 -> 108 to buy ascent margin (finding 2) and 108 is the top of what the doubling rule allows: the legal range is 86.3 to 143.9 kg. base_slots stays 6 because GDD 2.2 puts it on screen.

Finding 2, shipping_slice_reachable. The audit was right that the old ship was drag-limited rather than delta-v-limited, and measurement says the lever is exhaust velocity, not thrust: at thrust_n 5200 the flight model reaches 64,416 m of apex at fuel_burn_kgs 2.17 and 73,293 m at 1.73, on the same TWR. So the burn was stretched instead of enlarged. thrust_n 7000 over fuel_burn_kgs 2.0 is an exhaust velocity of 3,500 m/s; wet mass 108 + 360 = 468 kg gives ideal dv = 3500 * ln(468/108) = 3500 * 1.466 = 5,132 m/s against the old 1,892, and a 180 s burn against the old ~72 s, so most of it is spent above the dense air rather than against it. Liftoff TWR is 7000 / (468 * 9) = 1.66, barely moved from the old 1.62 — the fix is not thrust. Flown: the base ship's ballistic arc apexes at 73,759 m against a 65,000 m band floor with a 135 s EVA window and 26.5% of the tank left, and the circularised route also closes with 16.9% left. Both routes reach the middle and top samples too, which is more than the rule asks; see the note on what altitude is and is not gated by.

Finding 1, heavy_descent_requires_multi_pass. commit_floor_m stays at 8,000 m — 35 km below atmosphere_top_m 43,000 and 8 km above ground — and every peak below is the coolest legal single pass, entry pinned at that floor. Flown from the top of the band: empty 158.2, half hold 196.8, full hold 229.0, endgame haul (solar_wing_spine, 142.5 kg, the heaviest piece in the catalog) 241.0; the endgame haul at one skim is 161.0 and at two is 155.3. The satisfiable window for the whole capacity ladder is therefore [229.0, 241.0), and the ladder is now inside it: base heat_capacity 232, heat_shield tier 1 235, tier 2 238. The old ladder put 235 and 255 above the endgame peak of 224, which is exactly the 'a maxed shield buys the plunge back' failure. All three parts hold: the endgame haul cannot stay under any tier on one pass (241.0 > 238), it comes home on one skim (161.0 < 232), and an empty ship and a full hold still plunge from anywhere in the band (bottom 95.5 / 141, middle 122 / 178, top 158 / 229, all under 232).

Finding 1, the part I could not widen, stated because the next revision will hit it too. The window is 12.0 bar-units, 5.3% — and it is 5.3% at every commit floor I measured (2,000 m: 242.7 vs 255.7; 14,000 m: 211.1 vs 221.9), because peak heat goes as roughly the square root of ship mass and the endgame haul is only 10.9% heavier than a full hold (250.5 kg against 225.9 kg all-up). That is not a tuning choice: GDD 2.5 says a full hold roughly doubles the ship and GDD 2.6 says the module roughly doubles the ship, so the design's own prose puts them at the same mass and drives the window to zero. It is non-zero only because the catalog's heaviest piece happens to be 1.21x a full base hold. Three tiers fit at ~1.3% spacing and no re-pricing widens them; widening needs the endgame object to be heavier than a full hold, which is not a number I own.

GDD 2.2, the ablation model, evaluated rather than asserted. cost(sample,k) = SUM(i=0..k) 5.0 * 1.9^i + 7.0e-6 * (heat_index[sample] * skim_heat_multiplier[k])^3 + k * 7.0e-6 * 67^3. skim_heat_multiplier is the flown array from the top sample, [1.0, 0.377, 0.377, 0.377] — adopted exactly as the charter instructs, measured with the skim altitude scanned to 32,250 m and the entry depth held fixed, and flat after index 1 as the saturation rule requires. heat_index is the direct-entry peak on the same measurement basis the array came from: bottom 100.0 (the calibration point), middle 129.5, top 169.1. Cumulative tolls are 5.0 / 14.5 / 32.55 / 66.845 and each skim adds 7.0e-6 * 300,763 = 2.105. Top, term by term: entries 7.0e-6 * [169.1, 63.75, 63.75, 63.75]^3 = 33.85 / 1.81 / 1.81 / 1.81, skims 0 / 2.11 / 4.21 / 6.32, totals 38.85 / 18.42 / 38.57 / 74.97, minimum at index 1. Middle 20.20 / 17.42 / 37.58 / 73.98, minimum at 1. Bottom 12.00 / 16.98 / 37.14 / 73.54, minimum at 0. So the cheap end of the band plunges home and the top two thirds pay for a skim, and no sample's optimum exceeds the top's.

GDD 2.2, why heat_index is not the same number as the capacity ladder above it, since the last audit spotted the gap. heat_index is measured at entry depth 0 — a periapsis on the ground — because that is where the simulator's skim study measures skim_heat_multiplier, and the two have to share a basis or the product means nothing. The capacity ladder is measured at the commit floor, 8,000 m, because that is the shallowest entry the design lets a player fly. Same bar, two entry depths, and the direct entries run about 7% hotter at depth 0 (169.1 against 158.2 empty at the top). Neither figure is wrong; a periapsis-0 entry is simply not a legal descent, so it prices the skim model and does not set the capacity.

GDD 2.3, the parachute, stated as a canopy. parachute_area_m2 85 at parachute_drag_coefficient 1.5, against the Researcher's rho0 = 1.5 and g = 9.0, on the flown full-hold mass of 108 + 117.9 = 225.9 kg: v = sqrt(2 * 225.9 * 9.0 / (1.5 * 1.5 * 85)) = sqrt(4066.2 / 191.25) = sqrt(21.26) = 4.61 m/s. That is descent_speed_full_hold_ms, and the flight model integrates the same canopy to 4.61 m/s. It sits 0.39 m/s under the 5.0 soft line and well above 3.5, so the Parachute upgrade is a real purchase and not a formality.

Finding 3, nothing_satisfied_by_moving_the_target. The audit's substantive objection was that the storage counterweight had been relocated onto a parachute track the GDD does not sell, via a 65 -> 120 -> 260 m2 canopy that made each Storage tier soft-landable only with its matching Parachute tier. That coupling is gone: the base 85 m2 canopy lands every storage tier on its own — 6 slots 4.61 m/s, 8 slots 5.00, 10 slots 5.35 — so the worst maxed-hold landing is 0.35 m/s over the soft line, a graded hard landing rather than a gate. The canopy ladder is now 85 -> 105 -> 125 m2, a 1.47x over two tiers instead of 4x, and it buys margin (10 slots at 4.41 m/s) rather than permission. The parachute track itself I cannot remove: my charter and the params schema both require exactly six parts at two tiers with `parachute` among them, and both state that GDD 2.5's '4 parts x 3 tiers, parachute at fixed mid-tier' is superseded. Every other GDD-fixed number is untouched: base_slots 6, base_tether_slots 2, soft_landing_ms 5, cargo_damage_interval_s 3, heat_dissipation_s 5, no_gear_multiplier 2, magnet_range_screens 0.125.

Finding 3, the half of it I could not fix, raised as the blocking schema question the audit asked for rather than tuned around. GDD 2.5 assigns the storage counterweight to the heat shield, as 'the only purchase that reduces ship mass'. I cannot express that: an upgrade entry carries one `effect` string and one `value`, and my charter requires both heat_shield tiers to buy `heat_capacity` — 'Every tier must still sit below the satellite's single-pass peak, or a maxed shield buys the plunge back'. A shield tier that was both lighter and stronger needs two effects per entry, or a `dry_mass_delta_kg` field on the upgrade. Until the schema can say it, the shield tiers here buy capacity only and change no mass, and the storage difficulty curve is carried by mass and the landing grade rather than by any counterweight. Secondary, same shape: cargo.compactor_tier contradicts GDD 4.3's cut of the compactor and of size classes ('Every piece is one slot'), and I cannot set it to 0 because the schema floors it at 1. Both are routed, not worked around.

GDD 2.5, a lazy run breaks even. launch_cost 95 sits between two and three cheap pieces off the floor: with value_gradient interpolating 1.0 at 50,000 m to 5.5 at 280,000 m, a scorched_hull_panel at 52,000 m is 40 * 1.039 = 41.6, and the three cheapest non-fragile pieces near the floor are 41.6 + 56.4 + 62.7 = 160.7. A lazy six-slot bottom-band haul (two panels, a fuel bladder, an insulation bale, a bent truss) grosses 306.3 against 95 launch plus a flown 24.5% plate at replate_cost_per_pct 2 = 49, so 144 out and 306 in. Even a three-panel run that barely bothers grosses 124.7 against 117.2 and still clears. One intact fragile piece reshapes that completely: a cracked_solar_array at 63,000 m is 90 * 1.254 * 3.0 = 338.7, more than the whole lazy haul.

GDD 2.4, no shear under steady tow, as a bound rather than a sample. Steady cable tension is m_piece * a with a = jetpack_thrust_n / (suit_mass_kg + total towed), so tension = 240 * m / (110 + M), strictly under 240 N at every load and every tether count — mass suppresses acceleration faster than it loads the cable. magnet_hold_force_n is 900 N at base tier, a 3.75x margin everywhere. The heaviest legal two-piece tow in the catalog is scorched_reentry_cone 138 kg plus isotope_cask 132 kg: a = 240 / 380 = 0.632 m/s2 and the worst cable carries 87.2 N. Two mid-band pieces (135 kg) give 0.98 m/s2 against a bare suit's 2.18 — noticeably heavier, still flyable. Shear can therefore only fire on latch jerk and swing jerk, which is what GDD 2.4 says it is for.

Consequential knock-on I am flagging rather than hiding, because it is a genuine conflict between two artifacts and neither side can settle it alone. At dry_mass_kg 108 over the Researcher's reference_area_m2 3.5 and drag_coefficient_shield 1.4, the staged ballistic coefficient is 22 kg/m2, well under the 50 kg/m2 floor the baseline says erases an orbit on first contact with air. The Debris Designer saw this, rescaled every mass by 1.5, and recommended deriving dry_mass_kg from a maxed hold at about 1,150 kg. I cannot take that: the Designer's 1,159 kg is ten top-third pieces at their mean mass, while the crew's own full-hold arithmetic — spawn-weighted, shipping slice only, hand-tetherable only, crushed slots — reads 19.66 kg per slot, so a maxed ten-slot hold is 197 kg and a base hold is 117.9. The audited doubling rule then pins dry mass between 86 and 144 kg and there is no value that satisfies both. I took the audited rule and am reporting the beta. The same 108 kg also makes the ship lighter than the 110 kg suited astronaut flying it, which is the clearest symptom that the mass scale, not any parameter here, is what needs settling.

What altitude is actually gated by, since the reachability fix over-delivered and someone should decide whether that is acceptable. Measured across every purchasable tank and thruster combination (360/460/560 kg against 7,000/8,500/10,000 N), the base ship reaches all three sample altitudes by both routes, and no combination fails to. On this planet a ship light enough to hold TWR above 1 against a 3.5 m2 frontal area is also carrying 5,000 m/s of delta-v, so altitude cannot be gated by fuel at any price I can set — the tank and thruster tiers buy margin for the return leg, not reach. The endgame is gated thermally instead: heat_capacity 232 against a 241 endgame peak, and the hold mass that pushes a descent over it. That is consistent with GDD 2.6's 'reachable and landable only near full upgrades' on the landable half and not on the reachable half, and it is a design call rather than a number I should have quietly tuned.

What I did not touch, so the next audit stays interpretable: reentry.unstaged_heat_multiplier 3, off_retrograde_penalty 1, heat_dissipation_s 5 and cargo_damage_interval_s 3; the whole tow_fee block (zero inside 1,200 m, linear to exactly 0.5 at the 628,319 m half-circumference, never negative and never above the cap); every eva value; size_class_base_value, fragile_value_premium and repair_cost_per_pct; and soft_landing_ms, damage_per_ms_over, no_gear_multiplier and fragile_multiplier. value_gradient 1.0 -> 5.5 and the twelve upgrade prices moved only where the flight and capacity ladders above forced them.
catalog_concerns: solar_wing_spine, mass_kg 142.5, and the endgame slot generally. The sweep takes the heaviest catalog piece as the endgame haul, so this piece alone sets the upper edge of the heat-capacity window at 241.0 against a full hold's 229.0 — a 5.3% gap that has to hold three shield tiers. GDD 2.6's module is not a catalog entry and 'roughly doubles the ship' the same way GDD 2.5's full hold does, so as long as the heaviest piece is close to a full hold the window stays this narrow. If the Designer can put the top of the catalog further above a full base hold, the ladder gets room; nothing I price can create it.

size_classes.slots_crushed and slots_uncrushed across all three classes. GDD 4.3 cuts size classes and the compactor outright — 'Every piece is one slot; the satellite is simply very heavy' — but the catalog still carries a crushed/uncrushed slot pair per class and the params schema floors cargo.compactor_tier at 1, so I cannot express the cut. The per-slot mass this produces (19.66 kg/slot) is what sets dry_mass_kg through the doubling rule, so it is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

collapsed_antenna_dish, deployable_mast_cassette and solar_wing_spine, hand_tetherable false. Correct per the charter, but it means the three oversized pieces are unreachable in the shipping slice while solar_wing_spine is simultaneously the piece the sweep flies as the endgame haul. The endgame load is therefore an object the player cannot tether, which is fine as a mass proxy for Armstrong's module and confusing as anything else.
